title: Jassa Singh Refuses to Yield and Gurmukh Singh Gives Him a Horse

blocks.text: Jassa Singh Ahluwalia refuses to leave the field even after receiving many wounds and riding a horse that can barely move any farther. His stubbornness comes from honor rather than recklessness: he would rather die fighting than let the fleeing caravan think its leaders abandoned them.

Companions plead with him to withdraw before he is completely trapped, but he continues to resist the idea of retreat. The exchange sharpens into a moving act of service when Gurmukh Singh made Jassa Singh mount his own horse so the wounded chief could continue directing the struggle instead of being lost on foot.

That gesture preserves both leadership and morale in the middle of a collapsing battlefield. The page therefore turns a moment of near-disaster into an example of collective discipline, where one Singh yields his own advantage to keep the Panth's command intact.
